Please read this! It is an honest review!. Developers read this if you want to make your app actually worth it!!!!! 
(New Update! The app keeps quitting every time I get on. How is that helpful -1 star. And I can’t even lower it that low anymore!)
(Update: The app “doesn’t have any ads right now” when I am trying to get my food! Not helpful! -1 star. Also it forces you to watch an ad every time you start the app -1 star. Very frustrating for this to not be connected to Apple Watch, I know that it is simple to do because so many apps do it -1 star. I also see that a TON of people have asked for Apple Watch and Fitbit connectivity and that developers don’t listen! -1 star. I am not sorry for lowering my rating, initially a fun app though.) Ok so I have only played this game for like three days (under ten planets still) but it has been amazing. The fact that it is a time based game is both a blessing and a curse! I tried a game before this called pocket plants, but it encouraged me to sit around and tap all day rather than walk.(plus other issues with ridiculous currency that you have to pay for, I really appreciate that I can watch ads to get cubes if I don’t want to pay!) I do wish that the steps could be converted to cubes or tomatoes based on your current needs, or just that you could convert energy into the tomatoes or cubes as well. I also think that when you have a planet that finishes production it would have you feed it and then ask you whether you want to start production or upgrade, because when it says that my people are hungry I feel bad so I feed them, but then I can’t upgrade unless I spend energy or cubes. It would also be nice if I could link my Apple Watch to the game to collect steps. I really like that it doesn’t force you to watch ads (except for when I get on it will sometimes randomly force me to watch an ad), but they are optional to get stuff that is useful (I personally watch all the daily ads to get the stuff I need) but I would like more ad variety then just the same five ads over and over again. I know that free games usually need ads to pay for the developers needs, but I think it is creepy that the ads that are pop-up are for places in my city, I know I gave permission for location services, but that is to track my steps, not to give me ads for local shops. I would also like it if it would encourage me to walk a little more (that is the whole reason I got this after all.) Overall a great game but these features could up it to a whole new level! Thanks for taking the time to read and please consider these ideas!

reviews.text:
It’s fun but outdated. Look, it’s fun enough and I’ll probably continue playing, but I don’t know why the developers insist on not permitting fitness trackers. I can do an entire day’s worth of spring cleaning involving vacuuming, walking back and forth to do laundry, organizing, cleaning, etc, + running back and forth trying to tire out my high energy cat, but because I often wear exercise shorts indoors without phone-sized pockets, Walkr apparently thinks I’m sitting around all day. 
 
Hey Walkr devs, not everyone owns or wears cargo shorts or enjoys having a giant phone slapping their leg or carrying their physical phone all the time. One could even say that this app is kiiinda rather sexist considering the issue with women’s pockets and how this app is leaving a whole lot of household and childcare activity unattributed. 
 
Please get with the times, stop being low key sexist, and allow fitness trackers already. The people who are going to cheat are gonna cheat regardless (as we know from lessons with Pokemon Go). Not allowing fitness trackers literally only hurts honest players who want to utilise their day-to-day real life efforts as much as possible.
